newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to join EMU by 2001 at latest-Economy min.
newsitem.headline: Greece to join EMU by 2001 at latest-Economy min.

text.p: Greece is determined to participate in the third stage of European Monetary and Economic Union (EMU) by 2001 at the latest, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said.

"The goal is to secure high growth rates and our participation in the third stage of the European Economic and Monetary Union in 2000 or 2001 at the latest," Papandoniou told a conference on the Greek economy organised by the Economist.
"The Greek economy has entered a virtuous cycle of small budget deficits, low inflation and comparatively higher growth rates," he said.

Papandoniou noted that the country's budget deficit fell to 7.4 percent of GDP in 1996 from 14.4 percent in 1994 while the debt to GDP ratio stabilised in 1996 and inflation dropped to 6.0 percent year-on-year in March from 12.3 percent at the end of 1993.
"The budget deficit is expected to drop to 4.2 percent of GDP, public debt will fall to 109 percent of GDP in 1997 from 111.8 percent in 1996," he said.
GDP growth accelerated to 2.6 percent in 1996 from a negative 1.0 percent in 1993 and is projected to rise to 3.5 percent in 1997, he said.
